steps.body: Three mats are fewer than five cats. Pairing one mat with one cat leaves two cats unmatched, so five is more and three is fewer.
steps.narration: Three mats are fewer than five cats. Pairing one mat with one cat leaves two cats unmatched, so five is more and three is fewer.

widget.prompt: There are 6 hearts. Build the stars so there are MORE stars.

commonCounts.feedback: Six stars pair off exactly with six hearts; that is SAME, not more.
Five stars run out before the hearts do; that is FEWER, not more.

widget.missFeedback: Build one star per heart, then add at least one extra.
widget.successFeedback: Seven stars beat six hearts — pairing leaves one star standing alone.

predict.prompt: More stars than 6 hearts — what does pairing leave?
predict.reveal: More means the pairing cannot use up the stars; at least one stands unmatched.

cml.actionGoal: Pair the groups one to one, or place both numbers in the counting song, for kcm more fewer same.
invariants: Comparison rests on two facts that never move: pairing one to one leaves the bigger group with leftovers, and a number later in the counting song always names more — which is what kcm more fewer same uses.
misconceptions: Judging by how much space a group fills, by the size of the things in it, or by which number was written first.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: If one more joined the smaller group, would the pairing come out even?

widget.prompt: There are 8 stars and 7 hearts. Which statement is true?

options.label: More stars
options.feedback: Correct — 8 stars against 7 hearts; pairing one to one leaves stars unmatched.

options.label: They are equal
options.feedback: Equal needs the pairing to come out even; here one side is left holding extras (8 against 7).

options.label: More hearts
options.feedback: Pairing one to one uses every heart with stars to spare, so the hearts are not the larger group.

options.label: You cannot tell
options.feedback: You can always tell — pair the groups one to one and look at which side has leftovers.

widget.prompt: How does pairing one to one settle which group is bigger?

options.label: The side left with unmatched things is the bigger group
options.feedback: Correct — pairing uses the groups up together, so whatever remains unmatched is the surplus.

options.label: The side that finishes pairing first is bigger
options.feedback: Finishing first means running OUT first — that is the smaller group, not the bigger.

options.label: Pairing only works for equal groups
options.feedback: Pairing works on any two groups; unequal ones simply leave a remainder on one side.

options.label: The side with bigger things is bigger
options.feedback: Pairing compares counts, not sizes — one large thing still pairs with one small one.

widget.prompt: What number comes right after 14? Hop one and tap where you land.

commonLandings.feedback: 14 stops one complete hop too soon. Continue the final 1-unit hop to reach 15.
16 goes one complete hop too far. One hop from 14 lands on 15.

widget.missFeedback: Count 1 on from 14: you land on 15.
widget.successFeedback: 15 — one hop forward, and one hop later in the song always means greater.
widget.lowFeedback: Short of the landing — a single hop forward reaches 15.
widget.highFeedback: Past the landing — right after 14 means one hop, stopping on 15.

concept.body: More means leftovers on that side after pairing. Fewer means running out first. Same means the pairing comes out even.
